Subject: Cutover orchestration & onboarding map — SableCare

Hi Emily / Tom —

Great to be formalizing the post-signature plan. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that embeds the implementation milestones, canary plan, migration windows, and a proposed training cadence for ops and dev teams. High level:

- Week 0 (this week): admin kickoff, access & network checks (we need the IP allowlist and VPN route in place)
- Week 1–2: dedicated environment provisioning + baseline model verification (internal smoke + perf)
- Week 3: canary traffic (10% production) for 72 hours, regression evals and rollback window
- Week 4: staged migration (50% -> 100%) + user training sessions (2 x 90m)
- Week 6: full handover, runbook transfer, SLA sign-off

I've included a canary runbook and suggested training outline. Action items for SableCare in the spreadsheet: network allowlist, sample traffic signature, and confirmation of the sandbox dataset for evals.

Please flag any timeline conflicts — we can compress the canary phase to 48 hours if you need a faster cut.

Attachments: SableCare_MAP_v1.2.xlsx; canary_runbook.pdf; training-outline.md

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

Neha / Emily —

Quick technical clarifications from our infra team:

1) During canary, will the KV cache be isolated per-tenant? We need assurance that prefix caching won't leak dev keys into production traces.
2) For the migration window, do you require a DB read-only freeze or can we rely on a staged parity sync? We have nightly ETL tasks that complicate a full freeze.

If Redwood can provide an architecture diagram that shows network flows and where logs are written (and retention), that will help our security review.

Thanks,
Tom Hu
CTO | SableCare
tom.hu@sablecare.com

Subject: Re: Cutover orchestration & onboarding map — SableCare

Tom —

Answers inline:

1) KV cache isolation: yes — canaries will run in an isolated namespace with separate KV namespaces and keys. We will also enable token scoping (per-tenant) for the trial, and all canary traffic is tagged; logs are scrubbed of secrets before export. See canary_runbook.pdf (section 2.3) for details.

2) DB strategy: we recommend a staged parity sync rather than a hard freeze. We will run a delta sync during the canary and then schedule a short (15–30 minute) final cutover window at the 50%->100% step to reconcile outstanding writes. That avoids impacting nightly ETL. We flagged this in the MAP under Migration Risks.

Training & scheduling: Marissa — I'll hand the training deck to you; Sergio, please create the access tokens for the sandbox cluster and set the retention policy per SableCare's compliance ask (30 days by default, adjustable).

Neha — I'll prep the architecture/network diagram and drop a link to the Drive folder by EOD Monday.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
